findings.title: Editing a shift replaces its saved per-date rates
findings.scenario: Tom posts a pharmacist shift offering Sara $80 per hour for a particular date, above his $60 pharmacy guide. Later, Tom opens the shift to correct its description. The saved $80 rate is replaced by the calculated $60 guide, and saving the description also submits that lower rate.
findings.test_needed: Load an existing shift with an $80 per-date override and a $60 calculated guide; change only its description and assert the submitted rate remains $80.

owner_question.question: When Tom edits only the description of Sara's advertised $80 shift, what should happen to its rate?
options: Keep $80 unless Tom explicitly changes it
Ask Tom before replacing $80 with the current guide
Automatically replace it with the current guide (keep today's behaviour)

findings.title: Manual shift times revert to pharmacy opening hours
findings.scenario: Tom selects a date manually for his first shift entry at a pharmacy whose hours are 09:00–17:00. He changes the start to 10:00 because Sara is needed for a shorter shift. The form immediately restores 09:00, preventing him from keeping his chosen time through this entry flow.
findings.test_needed: With pharmacy hours 09:00–17:00 and no added or calendar-selected dates, select a manual date, enter 10:00–16:00, and assert those times survive effects and are added unchanged.

owner_question.question: When Tom chooses a shorter shift for Sara than the pharmacy's opening hours, what should the manual time fields do?
options: Keep Tom's times after explicit confirmation
Restore pharmacy opening hours automatically (keep today's behaviour)
